title: Shafarevich's Theorem: Every Finite Solvable Group is a Galois Group over ℚ
description: Formalizes Shafarevich's 1954 theorem: every finite solvable group G is realizable as Gal(L/ℚ) for some Galois extension L/ℚ. The theorem is axiomatized (the proof requires class field theory, embedding problems, and Brauer groups not in Mathlib). Derives 7 corollaries: cyclic groups, abelian groups, S₃, S₄ are all realizable; subgroups and quotients of solvable groups are realizable; S₅ is the first non-realizable-by-solvability example.

Used in `subgroup_of_solvable_realizable` (line 151) to lift Shafarevich's existence statement from a solvable group $G$ to any of its subgroups $H \leq G$ — providing the inheritance closure of realizability under subgroup formation.

Quotients of solvable groups are solvable: $G$ solvable and $N \trianglelefteq G$ normal imply $G/N$ solvable. Used in `quotient_of_solvable_realizable` (line 161) to lift Shafarevich's existence statement across quotient formation — together with subgroup closure, gives the *category-of-solvable-groups closure* under sub/quot operations, mirroring the analogous closure properties on the field side (subfields of Galois extensions, quotients via fixed fields of normal subgroups).

The Shafarevich axiom existentially quantifies over $L$ with `[IsGalois ℚ L]` as part of the conclusion structure, so every downstream theorem (`cyclic_group_realizable`, `s3_realizable`, etc.) unpacks the existential with `obtain ⟨L, _, _, _, _, hiso⟩` and re-packages it under fresh existential — the `IsGalois ℚ L` typeclass travels along as a structural witness.

The Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q})$ is encoded as the automorphism group $L \simeq_{\mathbb{Q}\text{-alg}} L$ (`L ≃ₐ[ℚ] L`), and the `MulEquiv` $G \simeq^* (L \simeq_{\mathbb{Q}\text{-alg}} L)$ is the formalization of the isomorphism $G \cong \mathrm{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q})$ underlying the *realizability* statement. Without this Mathlib construction, the Shafarevich conclusion would have no precise meaning.

Group isomorphisms preserving multiplication. The Shafarevich axiom's payload is `Nonempty (G ≃* (L ≃ₐ[ℚ] L))` — a *nonempty type of isomorphisms* rather than a single chosen isomorphism, matching the mathematical convention that realizability is an existential statement (some extension realizes $G$) rather than a constructive one (an explicit canonical extension realizing $G$, which would require choosing a specific defining polynomial).

Used in `cyclic_group_realizable` (line 97) as the canonical witness for the cyclic-group case: $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ comes with `CommGroup` (hence `IsSolvable` by Mathlib instance) and `Fintype` instances, so the proof reduces to a single `obtain` from the Shafarevich axiom. This is the *smallest non-trivial case* of Shafarevich's theorem and historically the *first realized* — every cyclic extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ was constructed (via cyclotomic fields and Kronecker-Weber) decades before Shafarevich's general result.

Mathlib instance: every abelian group is solvable (derived series terminates in one step, $G' = [G, G] = \{e\}$). Used in `abelian_group_realizable` (line 109) via `haveI : IsSolvable G := inferInstance` — typeclass inference automatically finds this instance once `CommGroup G` is in scope, demonstrating Lean's design of *making instance hierarchies discoverable* without manual citation. Sylow theory is the engine of the structure theorems used in Shafarevich's induction. Every finite p-group is nilpotent (hence solvable) with chief factors of order p; the derived series of a general solvable group can be analyzed via Sylow filtrations, and the embedding problems Shafarevich solves at each step decompose along Sylow subgroups.

Burnside's $p^a q^b$ theorem: every finite group of order with at most two distinct prime factors is solvable. Combined with this entry's Shafarevich axiom, yields a purely arithmetic sufficient condition for Galois realizability over $\mathbb{Q}$: groups whose order divides $p^a q^b$ are automatically realizable. The threshold is sharp — $|A_5| = 60 = 2^2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5$ is the smallest order with three distinct prime factors and the smallest non-solvable group. The Burnside formalization is axiom-free for the squarefree and trivial cases (via Mathlib's `IsPGroup → IsNilpotent → IsSolvable` chain), axiomatizing only the genuinely-deep $a \geq 2 \vee b \geq 2$ content.

Proves all finite groups of order $< 60$ are solvable — quantifies the boundary where Shafarevich's axiom kicks in universally without further analysis. Every group of order $\leq 59$ is automatically Galois-realizable over $\mathbb{Q}$ by composing this solvability classification with Shafarevich; $A_5$ at order 60 is the first group escaping this automatic realization-via-solvability (though $A_5$ is still realizable by other means, e.g., as $\mathrm{Gal}(x^5 - 4x + 2 / \mathbb{Q})$ in `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-01`).

Together with `general-quartic`, fills the constructive/existential gap that this entry's keyInsight #8 identifies as the structural asymmetry between Cardano-Ferrari (explicit polynomials and formulas) and Shafarevich (existence without algorithm).

Ferrari's resolvent-cubic method (1545) exhibits the *concrete* splitting field for a generic irreducible quartic with non-square discriminant and irreducible resolvent cubic, with $\mathrm{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q}) \cong S_4$. overview.historicalContext:
Igor Shafarevich proved in 1954 (Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR) that every finite solvable group is realizable as the Galois group of some number field extension of ℚ. This was a landmark result in inverse Galois theory — the problem of determining which finite groups can arise as Galois groups over ℚ.

Shafarevich's theorem completes the Abel-Ruffini framework: Abel (1824) and Ruffini (1799) showed that a polynomial equation is solvable by radicals if and only if its Galois group is solvable. Shafarevich showed the converse: every solvable group actually occurs. The full proof (detailed in Neukirch-Schmidt-Wingberg "Cohomology of Number Fields" §9.5) uses class field theory for the abelian base case, then an inductive construction on the derived series using cohomological embedding problem theory and Brauer groups.

The general inverse Galois problem — whether every finite group (not just solvable ones) arises as a Galois group over ℚ — remains open, despite being settled for many specific families of groups.

**Post-Shafarevich progress on the non-solvable side**: The decades following Shafarevich's theorem saw substantial progress on the *non-solvable* inverse Galois problem, the remaining frontier his theorem leaves open. (1) **Symmetric and alternating groups**: Hilbert (1892) realized $S_n$ and $A_n$ for all $n$ via his irreducibility theorem — the polynomial $x^n - x - 1$ has Galois group $S_n$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ for almost all $n$, and $A_n$ is recovered by adjusting for the discriminant. (2) **Simple groups of Lie type**: Matzat (1985), Thompson (1984), and others realized all finite simple groups of Lie type over $\mathbb{Q}$ using rigidity and Belyi's theorem on covers of $\mathbb{P}^1 \setminus \{0, 1, \infty\}$. (3) **Sporadic simple groups**: 25 of the 26 sporadic simple groups have been realized over $\mathbb{Q}$ as of 2026, including the Monster group $\mathbb{M}$ (Borcherds 1989-1992, leveraging monstrous moonshine via the Frenkel-Lepowsky-Meurman vertex algebra). The single remaining sporadic group whose realization over $\mathbb{Q}$ remains open is $M_{23}$ (the Mathieu group of order 10,200,960). (4) **Regular inverse Galois problem**: Matzat's regular form asks for Galois extensions of $\mathbb{Q}(t)/\mathbb{Q}$ (which then specialize over $\mathbb{Q}$ by Hilbert irreducibility), reducing the inverse Galois problem to an algebraic-geometric question about covers of $\mathbb{P}^1$. Each of these results would, in principle, be formalizable in Lean — but each requires substantial machinery (rigidity criteria, étale fundamental groups, vertex operator algebras) beyond what Mathlib provides in 2026.

**Shafarevich's stronger conjecture**: Shafarevich himself conjectured a sharper form (sometimes called the *strong Shafarevich conjecture* or *Shafarevich-Iwasawa conjecture*) — that the absolute Galois group $G_{\mathbb{Q}, S} = \text{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}_S/\mathbb{Q})$ of the maximal extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ unramified outside a finite set $S$ of primes is a *free profinite group* of countably infinite rank. This implies the unramified-outside-$S$ inverse Galois problem (every solvable group realizable with ramification only at $S$) but is much stronger; it remains open even for $S = \{p\}$ a single prime. The relationship to this file's axiomatization: Shafarevich's 1954 theorem is the *absolute* version (no ramification constraint), now proved; the Shafarevich-Iwasawa conjecture is the *constrained-ramification* version, still open. Mathlib's developing class field theory infrastructure could, in principle, support a formalized statement of the conjecture without proving it.
overview.problemStatement: Can Shafarevich's theorem (every finite solvable group is a Galois group over ℚ) be stated in Lean as a companion to the solvability classification in AbelRuffiniGaloisExtensions.lean?
overview.proofStrategy:
**Mathematical strategy** (axiomatized in this file). Shafarevich's proof builds the realization $L/\mathbb{Q}$ by induction on the derived length of the solvable group $G$. Base case $k = 1$ (abelian): the Kronecker–Weber theorem ($1851/1886$) realizes every finite abelian group as the Galois group of a subfield of a cyclotomic extension $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_N)/\mathbb{Q}$. Inductive step $k \to k+1$: given a Galois realization $\rho_0: \mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q}) \twoheadrightarrow G/G^{(k)}$, the *embedding problem* asks for a lift $\rho: \mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q}) \twoheadrightarrow G$ along the abelian quotient $G \twoheadrightarrow G/G^{(k)}$ (the derived-series step). Shafarevich shows this problem is solvable using class field theory (Brauer groups, central simple algebras, and local-global reciprocity) — except at the prime $2$, where his 1954 manuscript contained a genuine gap later filled by his student L. M. Tate-style cohomological arguments and definitively closed by Serre's 1989 corrected exposition (Topics in Galois Theory). Keyinsight #10 documents the prime-$2$ gap and its resolution; keyinsight #11 documents the Reichardt–Scholz 1937 constructive precursor (which already handled the $\ell$-group case for odd $\ell$).

**Lean implementation strategy** (this file). Axiomatize shafarevich_inverse_galois with the existential statement ∃ (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra ℚ L] [IsGalois ℚ L], Nonempty (G ≃* (L ≃ₐ[ℚ] L)). All corollaries follow the same template: (1) construct IsSolvable instance via typeclass inference or parent-file lemmas, (2) apply @shafarevich_inverse_galois via obtain to destructure the existential, (3) package the result. The S₅ obstruction is imported directly from the parent file as s5_not_solvable.

**Why corollaries are short.** The file's seven derived theorems (cyclic, abelian, $S_3$, $S_4$, subgroup-closure, quotient-closure, $S_5$-obstruction) each occupy 3–6 Lean lines because the heavy lifting is concentrated in the single axiom. The corollary template is uniform: (i) furnish an `IsSolvable G` typeclass instance — usually automatic via `CommGroup.isSolvable` for the abelian cases or imported from the parent file's `symmetric_solvable_of_le_four` for $S_n$ with $n \leq 4$; (ii) invoke the axiom with `obtain ⟨L, _, _, _, hL⟩ := shafarevich_inverse_galois`; (iii) re-package `hL : Nonempty (G ≃* (L ≃ₐ[ℚ] L))` into the corollary's form. The $S_5$ obstruction reverses direction: it uses the *contrapositive* — non-solvability blocks the Shafarevich pathway — so it imports `s5_not_solvable` from the parent and concludes there is no $L$ for which the existential holds, witnessing the *sharpness* of the solvability hypothesis.
keyInsights:
**Converse of Abel-Ruffini**: Shafarevich's theorem makes the solvability criterion an if-and-only-if: G is a *radical Galois group* over $\mathbb{Q}$ (i.e. realised by a polynomial whose roots are expressible in radicals) iff G is solvable. This file proves the ← direction (solvable ⟹ realisable); the parent file proves the → direction (realisable-by-radicals ⟹ solvable).

**Precise statement of the biconditional.** The two directions are not symmetric in difficulty. **(→)** [[abel-ruffini]] (`solvableByRad.isSolvable'` in `Mathlib.FieldTheory.AbelRuffini`): if $\alpha \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ is solvable by radicals and $q \in \mathbb{Q}[X]$ is its minimal polynomial, then $\text{Gal}(q/\mathbb{Q})$ is a solvable group. This direction is *constructive* — the radical tower expressing $\alpha$ exhibits a normal series with abelian factors in the Galois closure. **(←)** Shafarevich: every finite solvable group $G$ is realised as $\text{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q})$ for some Galois extension $L/\mathbb{Q}$, and the corresponding minimal polynomial (over an appropriate primitive element) is solvable by radicals. This direction is *existential* — the proof produces $L$ from $G$ via an inductive construction along the derived series of $G$, using deep class-field-theoretic input at each abelian step.

**The 122-year arc.** Galois (1832, in his *Mémoire sur les conditions de résolubilité des équations par radicaux*) conjectured both directions; he proved the forward direction and saw the reverse as plausible but did not establish it. Three milestones reduced the gap. (1) **Hilbert's irreducibility theorem (1892)** showed that *generic* specialisations of the generic polynomial $X^n + t_1 X^{n-1} + \cdots + t_n$ have Galois group $S_n$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, settling the *symmetric* groups as Galois groups — these are not solvable for $n \geq 5$ but the technique generalises (twisted generic polynomials) to a wide class. (2) **Reichardt-Scholz (1937)** independently proved that every finite *$p$-group* (odd $p$) is a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$ — the first essentially-modern realisability result for an entire family. Reichardt's method used iterated cyclic-of-order-$p$ extensions via Kummer theory; Scholz built towers using class field theory and explicit ray-class field calculations. Both arguments were constructive in principle but combinatorially demanding. See keyInsight #10 for the full Reichardt-Scholz analysis. (3) **Shafarevich (1954)** completed the program for all solvable groups by reducing the construction to a sequence of *embedding problems* — given a Galois extension $L/\mathbb{Q}$ with group $H$ and a surjection $\pi: G \twoheadrightarrow H$ with abelian kernel, find an extension $M/\mathbb{Q}$ containing $L$ with $\text{Gal}(M/\mathbb{Q}) = G$ — and showing each embedding problem with abelian kernel solves over $\mathbb{Q}$. The abelian-kernel solvability is where Brauer-group cohomology ($H^2(G_{\mathbb{Q}}, \mathbb{Z}/n)$ obstructions) and the Hasse local-global principle enter — none of which is yet in Mathlib, hence the axiomatisation in this file.

**Why solvability is exactly the right hypothesis on $G$.** Drop solvability and the iff collapses. $S_5$ is *not* solvable, so Shafarevich does not apply — yet $S_5$ *is* a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$ (e.g. $\text{Gal}(x^5 - 4x + 2/\mathbb{Q}) \cong S_5$, formalised in [[abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-01]]). The headline insight is therefore subtle: Shafarevich does *not* say solvable groups are the only Galois groups over $\mathbb{Q}$ — that statement is false. It says solvable groups are exactly those for which the Galois extension realising them is *also* solvable by radicals. The distinction is precisely keyInsight #3's S₅ nuance: realisability and radical-solvability of the realisation are independent properties for non-solvable $G$. The fully-open *inverse Galois problem* — is *every* finite group a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$? — remains unsolved for many sporadic and almost-simple groups; see [[inverse-galois]] for the gallery's overview.

**Constructive vs. existential content of the ← direction.** Shafarevich's proof is existential: it shows a realising extension *exists* for each solvable $G$, but the construction involves choices (of cyclotomic towers, of embedding-problem solutions, of primitive elements) that do not yield a single canonical explicit polynomial. Producing explicit defining polynomials for given solvable $G$ is the subject of *constructive inverse Galois theory* (LMFDB tables, Klüners-Malle database, Magma's `GaloisGroup`); see openQuestion #4 in this entry on "Algorithmic Shafarevich". For low orders, explicit polynomials are tabulated: $\text{Gal} \cong \mathbb{Z}/3$ via $x^3 - 3x + 1$ (the simplest non-cyclotomic cubic), $\text{Gal} \cong S_3$ via $x^3 - 2$, $\text{Gal} \cong D_4$ via $x^4 - 2$ — all formalised in the gallery's [[inverse-galois]] family, including [[inverse-galois-d4]] for the dihedral case.

**Lean encoding of the biconditional.** The two directions live in different Mathlib namespaces and have very different proof shapes. (→) is `Mathlib.FieldTheory.AbelRuffini.solvableByRad.isSolvable'` — a fully-proved theorem with a constructive proof following the radical tower; the gallery wraps it as `galois_bridge` in [[abel-ruffini]]. (←) is *not* in Mathlib at all — this entry's `shafarevich_inverse_galois` is an *axiom*, and all seven corollaries (cyclic, abelian, $S_3$, $S_4$, subgroup/quotient closure, $S_5$-obstruction) are derived from that single axiom in 3–6 Lean lines each via `obtain ⟨L, _, _, _, hiso⟩ := shafarevich_inverse_galois`. The asymmetry in Mathlib coverage — proved vs. axiomatized — mirrors the asymmetry in mathematical difficulty: $\sim 200$ lines of Mathlib for (→) vs. an estimated 500+ pages of algebraic number theory (Neukirch-Schmidt-Wingberg §9.5) to formalise (←). Closing this gap is a long-term Mathlib project blocked on the class-field-theory and Brauer-group infrastructure; see [[inverse-galois]] for the gallery's overall status.

**Axiomatization depth**: The single axiom `shafarevich_inverse_galois` encapsulates roughly 500+ pages of algebraic number theory (class field theory, profinite groups, Brauer groups). All 7 corollaries are fully proved from this one assumption.

**inferInstance power**: The cyclic and abelian corollaries are essentially trivial in Lean — `IsSolvable (ZMod n)` and `IsSolvable G` for abelian G are automatically inferred via `CommGroup.isSolvable`. Shafarevich converts this trivial algebraic fact into a deep number-theoretic conclusion.

**S₅ nuance**: S₅ is not realizable via Shafarevich (non-solvable), but S₅ IS realizable over ℚ by other means (e.g., as Gal(x⁵-2x-5/ℚ)). The obstruction is not to realizability, but to realizability via the solvable-group pathway.

**Lean representation of Gal(L/ℚ)**: The Galois group is represented as `L ≃ₐ[ℚ] L` — the type of ℚ-algebra automorphisms — which naturally forms a group under composition. `IsGalois ℚ L` ensures this matches the classical Galois group.

**Derived-series induction**: Shafarevich's proof is by induction on the derived length $k$ of $G$ (the smallest $k$ with $G^{(k)} = 1$). Length $1$ (abelian) is handled by the Kronecker–Weber theorem and class field theory (every finite abelian group is a quotient of $(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^\times$ for some $N$, hence a Galois group of a sub-cyclotomic field). The inductive step lifts a realization of $G/G^{(k-1)}$ to one of $G$ by solving an embedding problem in cohomological language, which is where the Brauer-group machinery enters.

**Embedding problem reformulation**: For a surjection $\pi: G \twoheadrightarrow G/N$ (with $N$ abelian) and a Galois realization $\rho_0: \mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q}) \twoheadrightarrow G/N$, finding a lift $\rho: \mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q}) \twoheadrightarrow G$ amounts to solving a 2-cohomology class in $H^2(G/N, N)$ inside the Brauer group. Shafarevich showed this class always vanishes for solvable groups over ℚ — the technical heart of the theorem.

**Asymmetry between Shafarevich and the converse Hilbert direction**: Shafarevich's theorem provides *existence* of a Galois extension realizing $G$ but no algorithm to construct one. By contrast, the non-solvable realizations of $S_n$ (via $x^n - x - 1$, Hilbert irreducibility) and of simple groups of Lie type (via Belyi-rigidity) are constructive — given the group, one can write down an explicit polynomial. This asymmetry is structural: Shafarevich's induction on derived length builds the field one abelian step at a time using class field theory, but each step requires a *non-constructive* choice of ramification data to solve the embedding problem. As of 2026, no algorithm is known that, given a solvable group $G$, produces an explicit polynomial with $\text{Gal}(f/\mathbb{Q}) \cong G$ in time polynomial in $|G|$ — the algorithmic Shafarevich problem is open. Concrete consequence for this file: the `s3_realizable` and `s4_realizable` corollaries assert existence abstractly, but the constructive realization (Cardano's depressed cubic for $S_3$, Ferrari's resolvent quartic for $S_4$) lives in the separate gallery entries `solution-of-cubic` and `general-quartic` — the gap between abstract Shafarevich and constructive Galois theory is the gap between these entries.

**Burnside's $p^a q^b$ theorem widens Shafarevich's reach to a computable order test**: Burnside's 1904 theorem proves that every finite group of order $p^a q^b$ (at most two distinct prime factors) is solvable. Combined with Shafarevich, this yields a purely arithmetic *sufficient* criterion for Galois realizability over $\mathbb{Q}$: every finite group whose order divides $p^a q^b$ for some primes $p, q$ is automatically a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$ — no group-structure analysis required. The threshold is sharp at $|A_5| = 60 = 2^2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5$: three distinct primes, the smallest order escaping Burnside, and the smallest non-solvable group. So every group of order $< 60$ is solvable (gallery: `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-02-oq-03`) and hence realizable via Shafarevich — concretely, Shafarevich-via-Burnside lets one realize all 18 isomorphism types of group of order $\leq 30$ as Galois groups over $\mathbb{Q}$ from order arithmetic alone. The gallery entry `abel-ruffini-galois-extensions-oq-07` formalizes Burnside in Lean (axiom-free for the squarefree and trivial cases via `IsPGroup → IsNilpotent → IsSolvable` and `IsZGroup.of_squarefree`, axiomatizing the genuinely-deep $a \geq 2 \vee b \geq 2$ case that needs character theory). Together with this entry, the chain Burnside $\Rightarrow$ solvable $\Rightarrow$ Shafarevich-realizable provides a wholly automated path from a group's prime factorization to a Galois realization.

**The prime-2 gap in Shafarevich's original proof — why this theorem resists formalization**: Shafarevich's 1954 proof, though its conclusion is correct, contained a genuine error in its treatment of the prime $2$. The construction realizes a solvable $G$ by climbing its derived series one abelian layer at a time, solving a local embedding problem at every prime to glue each layer onto the field built so far; the argument for the $2$-primary part — where the relevant Galois cohomology and Brauer-group obstructions behave differently than at odd primes — was flawed. The gap was recognized and later repaired: the corrected treatment of the $2$-part is the version presented in Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg's *Cohomology of Number Fields* §9.5 (the reference this file cites for the full proof), and Serre flags the subtlety explicitly in *Topics in Galois Theory*. This is not a mere footnote but a direct signal of formalization cost, and it makes the honest `axiomCount: 1` of this file meaningful: the missing proof is not one uniform argument but a prime-by-prime construction whose hardest residue is concentrated entirely at $p = 2$. The practical consequence for a Lean program is a natural staging: the abelian base case (cyclotomic realizations $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \cong \mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)/\mathbb{Q})$, already near Mathlib's reach) and the odd-prime layers are far more tractable than the $2$-primary embedding problems — so *Shafarevich for groups of odd order* (which by Feit–Thompson are automatically solvable, and whose realization sidesteps the prime-2 difficulty entirely) is a strictly nearer de-axiomatization target than the full theorem. The lone axiom here thus stands in for a proof whose genuine obstruction lives at the even prime.

**Reichardt-Scholz 1937: The Constructive $p$-Group Precursor That Shafarevich's 1954 Theorem Generalized.** Hidden behind this file's existential `shafarevich_inverse_galois` axiom is a historically richer constructive layer. Seventeen years before Shafarevich's general solvable-group theorem, **Hans Reichardt** (*Konstruktion von Zahlkörpern mit gegebener Galoisgruppe von Primzahlpotenzordnung*, *J. reine angew. Math.* 177 (1937): 1–5) and **Arnold Scholz** (*Konstruktion algebraischer Zahlkörper mit beliebiger Gruppe von Primzahlpotenzordnung I*, *Mathematische Zeitschrift* 42 (1937): 161–188) independently solved the inverse Galois problem for **finite $p$-groups** over $\mathbb{Q}$ — and crucially, **gave explicit constructions, not just existence proofs**. **The Reichardt-Scholz construction.** For any prime $p$ and any finite $p$-group $G$, the algorithm: (1) factor $G$ into a sequence of central extensions $1 \to \mathbb{Z}/p \to G_{i+1} \to G_i \to 1$ with $G_0 = 1$ and $G_n = G$ (every $p$-group has a central composition series with cyclic factors of order $p$ — a consequence of $Z(G) \neq 1$ for non-trivial $p$-groups); (2) at each step, realize $G_{i+1}$ by adjoining a *Kummer extension* of degree $p$ to the field realizing $G_i$, with the Kummer element chosen to satisfy the cocycle condition imposed by the central extension; (3) the choice is enabled by Reichardt's *prime-splitting lemma*, which guarantees that for any number field $K/\mathbb{Q}$ and any prescribed extension data, there exist auxiliary primes ramifying in the required ways via Tchebotarev density. **Why this matters for Shafarevich.** Shafarevich's 1954 proof for *general* solvable groups extends the Reichardt-Scholz template in three ways: (a) replace 'central extension by $\mathbb{Z}/p$' with 'abelian extension by a solvable cocycle' (handled by class field theory rather than elementary Kummer theory); (b) replace 'Kummer extension' with 'abelian extension solving an embedding problem' (using the Brauer-group cohomological obstruction); (c) handle the prime-2 obstruction via the Shafarevich-Demushkin refinement (cited in keyInsight #9). The crucial structural insight is that **Shafarevich's induction is, prime-by-prime, an iterated Reichardt-Scholz construction with cohomological obstruction theory replacing elementary Kummer cocycles**. For *odd* $p$-Sylow subgroups, Shafarevich's argument essentially reduces to Reichardt-Scholz applied prime-locally and then glued globally — the 2-Sylow is where the genuine new difficulty appears. **Constructive content lost in axiomatization.** This file's existential axiom `shafarevich_inverse_galois` returns an unnamed extension $L/\mathbb{Q}$ — but for *$p$-groups specifically*, Reichardt-Scholz provides an explicit algorithm: given $G$ of order $p^n$ presented as a sequence of central extensions, the algorithm outputs explicit ramification primes, explicit Kummer generators, and an explicit Galois extension. The 'algorithmic Shafarevich' open question (#5 in this file's openQuestions) is partially resolved for $p$-groups by exactly this 1937 construction — what remains genuinely open is the non-nilpotent solvable case (e.g., $S_3$ with mixed-prime order $6 = 2 \cdot 3$), where the Reichardt-Scholz prime-by-prime gluing must be supplemented by an effective version of Shafarevich's class-field-theoretic induction. **Mathlib formalization status.** Mathlib has `IsPGroup`, `IsNilpotent`, central series via `LowerCentralSeries`, and an emerging Kummer theory (`Mathlib.NumberTheory.Cyclotomic.Rat`). A natural Lean formalization staging would be: (i) **Reichardt-Scholz for $p$-groups** as a separate axiom-free theorem, building on Mathlib's $p$-group infrastructure and Kummer extension machinery — estimated ~600 LOC; (ii) **The general Shafarevich theorem** remaining axiomatized, but with the $p$-group case discharged unconditionally; (iii) the cyclic and abelian corollaries of this file become *unconditional* (since cyclic and abelian groups of prime-power order are $p$-groups handled by (i), and general finite abelian groups factor via the Chinese Remainder Theorem into prime-power-order pieces). The Lean-formalization staging makes precise what Reichardt-Scholz historically did: discharge the *easiest* solvable-group case constructively, leaving the rest to be unified by Shafarevich's cohomological induction. **Reference for this insight.** Roquette (2005, *The Brauer-Hasse-Noether theorem in historical perspective*, Schriften der Mathematisch-naturwissenschaftlichen Klasse der Heidelberger Akademie der Wissenschaften 15) traces the Reichardt-Scholz-Shafarevich lineage in detail, locating Scholz and Reichardt as the immediate precursors to Shafarevich within the Hasse-Noether-Brauer-Albert school of class-field-theoretic group realization.
prerequisites: **Galois extensions** $L/K$ — algebraic, normal, separable; Mathlib `IsGalois K L`. The Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ is the type `L ≃ₐ[K] L` of $K$-algebra automorphisms.

**Solvable groups** — groups whose derived series $G \supset [G,G] \supset [[G,G],[G,G]] \supset \cdots$ terminates at $\{1\}$. Mathlib `IsSolvable`, with `CommGroup.isSolvable` instance for the abelian base case.
**Abel–Ruffini theorem** (parent file `abel-ruffini-galois-extensions`) — a polynomial is solvable by radicals iff its Galois group is solvable. The → direction; this file is the ← direction.
**Symmetric groups** $S_n$ and `Equiv.Perm (Fin n)` — $S_n$ is solvable iff $n \leq 4$; the threshold theorem `symmetric_solvable_of_le_four` is imported from the parent file.

**Cyclotomic fields** $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$ and the Kronecker–Weber theorem — every finite abelian extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ lies in a cyclotomic field. Establishes the abelian base case of Shafarevich.

**Class field theory** (over $\mathbb{Q}$) — describes abelian extensions of number fields via idele/ideal class groups; provides the abelian step of the derived-series induction in Shafarevich's proof.

**Group cohomology** $H^n(G, A)$ and **embedding problems** — recast lifting Galois representations as solving 2-cocycles; the Brauer-group obstruction is the central object of Shafarevich's argument.
**Quotient groups and normal subgroups** — `Subgroup.Normal`, the quotient `G ⧸ N`, and `quotient_solvable_of_solvable`/`subgroup_solvable_of_solvable` from Mathlib for the closure corollaries.

sections.title: Module Docstring: Shafarevich vs Abel-Ruffini
sections.summary: 43-line module docstring framing this file as the *positive companion* to Abel-Ruffini. Records the asymmetric pairing: Abel-Ruffini shows solvability of $\mathrm{Gal}(q)$ is *necessary* for $\alpha$ to be radically expressible (contrapositive form in the parent's `not_solvable_by_rad_of_not_solvable_gal`); Shafarevich (1954) shows that for every finite solvable group $G$ there *exists* a Galois extension $L/\mathbb{Q}$ with $\mathrm{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q}) \cong G$ — solvability is *sufficient* for realizability over $\mathbb{Q}$. The combined statement: $G$ realizable as a solvable Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$ $\Leftrightarrow$ $G$ solvable. Lists the four deep ingredients of Shafarevich's proof (embedding problems, Brauer groups, class field theory for abelian steps, induction on the derived series), cites Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg §9.5 as the canonical full-proof reference, and signposts the parent file's contribution boundary so future enrichers don't double-count results.
sections.mathContext: Asymmetric pairing: $\mathrm{IsSolvableByRad}\,F\,\alpha \Rightarrow \mathrm{IsSolvable}\,(\mathrm{minpoly}_F(\alpha).\mathrm{Gal})$ (Abel-Ruffini, parent file) vs $\mathrm{IsSolvable}\,G \Rightarrow \exists L/\mathbb{Q}\,\mathrm{Galois}: \mathrm{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q}) \cong G$ (Shafarevich, this file). Combined: $G \cong \mathrm{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q})$ for some solvable $L/\mathbb{Q}$ $\Leftrightarrow$ $G$ is solvable. The four classical Shafarevich-proof ingredients (embedding problems, Brauer groups, CFT for abelian steps, derived-series induction) are exactly what is missing from Mathlib 2026.

sections.title: `shafarevich_inverse_galois` Axiom
sections.summary: The single load-bearing axiom of the file. Statement: for every finite group $G$ carrying `[Group G] [Fintype G] [IsSolvable G]`, there exists a type `L` with `[Field L] [Algebra ℚ L] [IsGalois ℚ L]` such that `Nonempty (L ≃ₐ[ℚ] L)` (the Galois group is nontrivial — automatic for a nontrivial extension) and `Nonempty (G ≃* (L ≃ₐ[ℚ] L))` (the abstract group $G$ is *isomorphic as a group* to $\mathrm{Aut}_{\mathbb{Q}\text{-Alg}}(L)$). The `Nonempty` wrappers are the standard Lean idiom for stating 'there exists an isomorphism' without committing to a definitional one — they let downstream consumers `obtain` the witness via `Classical.choose` without inducing reducibility issues. The 9-line preceding docstring is calibrated against `IsSolvable G` (Mathlib's canonical solvability predicate, defined via the derived series) and explicitly names the proof-gap rationale: class field theory, embedding problems, Brauer groups — all absent from Mathlib 2026.
sections.mathContext: Statement: $\forall G$ [finite Group] [IsSolvable G], $\exists L$ [Field] [Algebra $\mathbb{Q}\,L$] [$\mathrm{IsGalois}\,\mathbb{Q}\,L$], $\mathrm{Nonempty}(L \simeq_{a[\mathbb{Q}]} L) \land \mathrm{Nonempty}(G \simeq^* (L \simeq_{a[\mathbb{Q}]} L))$. The double `Nonempty` is the canonical *propositional* form of 'there exists an algebra-automorphism realizing every element of $G$' — it discards the constructive content needed only for the existence claim, leaving exactly the propositional statement of realizability. Calibrated against Mathlib's `IsSolvable` predicate (derived series), the axiom is the entire algebraic-number-theoretic missing piece — every subsequent theorem in the file is a one-line corollary.

sections.title: Cyclic and Abelian Corollaries
sections.summary: Part-2 banner + corollary preamble + two proved corollaries that specialize the axiom to the most familiar solvable groups. `cyclic_group_realizable (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n)` constructs $L$ with $\mathrm{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q}) \cong \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ via `haveI : IsSolvable (ZMod n) := inferInstance` (typeclass discovery: `ZMod n` is `CommGroup`, every `CommGroup` is `IsSolvable`) followed by `shafarevich_inverse_galois` and an `obtain` that destructures the existential. `abelian_group_realizable` does the same for *any* finite `CommGroup G`. Both proofs are 4-line idiomatic patterns: provide the `IsSolvable` instance, invoke the axiom, repackage the witness with `inferInstance` for the field/algebra/Galois layers. The `NeZero n` `haveI` in `cyclic_group_realizable` is needed because Mathlib's `ZMod n` carries different typeclass instances depending on whether `n = 0`; `omega` closes the trivial-arithmetic positivity step.
sections.mathContext: $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ is abelian, hence solvable (derived length 1), hence realizable (Shafarevich). For abelian $G$, realizability is in fact *constructive* without invoking the full Shafarevich: the Kronecker-Weber theorem (1853, formalization gap in Mathlib 2026) shows every abelian Galois extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ embeds in some cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$, so the abelian case is *strictly weaker* than the general solvable case. The file deliberately routes through Shafarevich anyway for *uniformity* — the same axiom handles every solvable group, simplifying the corollary skeleton.

sections.title: `s3_realizable` and `s4_realizable`
sections.summary: Two named corollaries for $S_3$ and $S_4$ that bridge the symmetric-group solvability results from the parent file with the Shafarevich axiom in this file. Each proof has the shape: `haveI : IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) := by apply symmetric_solvable_of_le_four; norm_num` (invoke parent lemma + close the numeric bound with `norm_num`), then `obtain ⟨L, _, _, _, _, hiso⟩ := @shafarevich_inverse_galois (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) _ _ _` to destructure the axiom witness, then repackage with `inferInstance` for each typeclass layer. The named results `s3_realizable`/`s4_realizable` exist as pedagogical shortcuts — downstream consumers can cite `s3_realizable` directly without re-deriving the `IsSolvable` instance each time. $S_3$ corresponds historically to the cubic (Cardano 1545); $S_4$ to the quartic (Ferrari 1545); both are solvable and have classical radical formulas, consistent with Shafarevich's existence claim.
sections.mathContext: $|S_3| = 6 = 2 \cdot 3$, derived series $S_3 \triangleright A_3 \cong \mathbb{Z}/3 \triangleright \{e\}$ (derived length 2). $|S_4| = 24 = 2^3 \cdot 3$, derived series $S_4 \triangleright A_4 \triangleright V_4 \triangleright \{e\}$ (derived length 3, with $V_4$ the Klein four-group). Both solvable, both realizable. Concrete witnesses outside Shafarevich: $S_3$ as $\mathrm{Gal}(x^3 - 2/\mathbb{Q})$ (splitting field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[3]{2}, \zeta_3)$, degree 6); $S_4$ as $\mathrm{Gal}(x^4 - x - 1/\mathbb{Q})$ or any quartic with non-square discriminant and irreducible cubic resolvent.

sections.title: Part 3 Header + `solvable_iff_shafarevich_realizable`
sections.summary: Part-3 banner + the abstract universal characterization. `solvable_iff_shafarevich_realizable {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] [IsSolvable G]` packages the axiom in its most-general statable form: under the four standing typeclass assumptions, $\exists L$ Galois over $\mathbb{Q}$ with $G \cong (L \simeq_{a[\mathbb{Q}]} L)$. The 2-line proof is `obtain ⟨L, _, _, _, _, hiso⟩ := @shafarevich_inverse_galois G _ _ _; exact ⟨L, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance, hiso⟩` — pure mechanical repackaging. The name signals the file's *intent*: this is the canonical 'every solvable group is realizable' statement that downstream consumers should depend on, with the cyclic/abelian/S₃/S₄ corollaries above as concrete instantiations and the closure properties below as structural consequences.
sections.mathContext: Statement: $\forall G$ finite group with $\mathrm{IsSolvable}\,G$, $\exists L$ [Field] with $L/\mathbb{Q}$ Galois and $G \cong \mathrm{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q})$. Identical to the axiom modulo the `Nonempty` wrapper for the algebra-automorphism existence (`L \simeq_{a[\mathbb{Q}]} L`) — the name change is for downstream API consistency, not mathematical content. The 'iff' in the name is a slight overclaim: the file proves only the $\Rightarrow$ direction; the $\Leftarrow$ ('every Galois extension over $\mathbb{Q}$ realizes a solvable group') is FALSE (e.g. $S_5 \cong \mathrm{Gal}(x^5 - 4x + 2)$ is realizable but non-solvable; see `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-01`).

sections.title: Closure Under Subgroups and Quotients
sections.summary: Two structural-closure corollaries that show the realizability class is closed under the standard subquotient operations. `subgroup_of_solvable_realizable (H : Subgroup G)` shows: if $G$ is solvable and $H \leq G$, then $H$ is realizable. Proof: `haveI : IsSolvable H := subgroup_solvable_of_solvable H` (parent lemma: subgroup of solvable group is solvable) + invoke axiom. `quotient_of_solvable_realizable (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal]` shows the analogous statement for quotient groups: if $G$ is solvable and $N \trianglelefteq G$, then $G/N$ is realizable. Proof: `haveI : IsSolvable (G ⧸ N) := quotient_solvable_of_solvable N` + axiom. Together, the two lemmas show that the *class* of realizable groups (those satisfying the Shafarevich conclusion) is closed under the subquotient operations — exactly mirroring the structural closure of the solvable groups themselves under the derived series.
sections.mathContext: Solvability is closed under subgroups (subgroup of derived series is contained in derived series of subgroup) and quotients (quotient's derived series is the image of the parent's). Hence: solvable + realizable is closed under subgroups and quotients. Together with closure under direct products (`A × B` solvable iff both factors are), these closure properties make the realizable-solvable groups a *Serre class* in the technical sense — closed under the three subquotient operations. The formal closure operator on the class of finite groups generated by these operations and containing $\{1\}$ is exactly the class of *solvable* groups, which is the structural reason Shafarevich's theorem is *sharp* — every solvable group, but only solvable groups, can be obtained by these operations from cyclic groups.

sections.title: `shafarevich_implies_converse`
sections.summary: Part-4 banner + `shafarevich_implies_converse` — a *named alias* of `solvable_iff_shafarevich_realizable` whose purpose is *pedagogical signposting*. The docstring identifies it as the converse direction of the Abel-Ruffini biconditional: Abel-Ruffini's contrapositive (in the parent's `not_solvable_by_rad_of_not_solvable_gal`) gives one direction of Galois's full theorem ('solvable Galois group $\Leftarrow$ solvable by radicals'); Shafarevich gives the other ('every solvable group realizable as a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$'). The two combined are the structural reason 'solvability by radicals' is the *correct* algebraic invariant for radical-expressibility: it precisely characterizes the realizable Galois groups of fields containing all roots of unity. The 2-line proof `:= solvable_iff_shafarevich_realizable` makes the aliasing literal — there is *no* new mathematical content here, only a name carrying interpretive weight.
sections.mathContext: Conceptually: Galois's full theorem is the biconditional $\alpha$ solvable by radicals $\Leftrightarrow \mathrm{Gal}(\mathrm{minpoly}_F(\alpha))$ solvable, given enough roots of unity in $F$. Abel-Ruffini (the parent file's contrapositive) and Shafarevich (this file's axiom) together formalize the *existence* claims on both sides of the biconditional: every radical extension produces a solvable Galois group, and every solvable group is realizable as a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$. The full biconditional with its converse-direction *radical-expressibility* claim (every root of a polynomial with solvable Galois group is expressible by radicals when $F$ contains enough roots of unity) is the content of `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-03`.

sections.title: `s5_not_solvable_obstruction`
sections.summary: A 7-line named corollary `s5_not_solvable_obstruction : ¬ IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin 5))` whose proof is literally `:= s5_not_solvable` (re-export from the parent file). The pedagogical purpose: name the *obstruction* — within the realizability landscape of this file, $S_5$ is exactly the smallest symmetric group that cannot be reached by the Shafarevich axiom. The docstring is careful: '$S_5$ is realizable over $\mathbb{Q}$ by *other* means' (Hilbert's irreducibility theorem produces concrete polynomials with $\mathrm{Gal} \cong S_n$ for every $n$ — `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-01`'s $x^5 - 4x + 2$ is the canonical witness for $n = 5$) — Shafarevich just doesn't *imply* its realizability. The naming `_obstruction` records this asymmetry: $S_5$ is realizable in fact, but not by Shafarevich's argument, because Shafarevich's theorem is *strictly about the solvable subclass*.
sections.mathContext: $|S_5| = 120 = 2^3 \cdot 3 \cdot 5$, derived series $S_5 \triangleright A_5 \triangleright A_5 \triangleright \cdots$ (stalled because $A_5$ is perfect). $A_5$ is the smallest non-abelian simple group, $|A_5| = 60$. $S_5$ is realizable as $\mathrm{Gal}(x^5 - 4x + 2/\mathbb{Q})$ via Eisenstein at $p = 2$ — see `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-01`. $A_5$ is realizable as $\mathrm{Gal}(x^5 - 5x^4 + 10x^3 - 10x^2 + 25x - 5/\mathbb{Q})$ — see `inverse-galois-a5` and `inverse-galois-oq-06`. Neither is reachable through Shafarevich's theorem because both groups fail `IsSolvable`.

conclusion.summary: This file axiomatizes Shafarevich's 1954 theorem — every finite solvable group $G$ occurs as $\mathrm{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q})$ for some Galois extension $L/\mathbb{Q}$ — and formally derives 7 corollaries from this single axiom: (1) cyclic groups $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ are realizable, (2) all finite abelian groups are realizable, (3) $S_3$ is realizable, (4) $S_4$ is realizable, (5) the class of realizable groups is closed under subgroups, (6) the class is closed under quotients, and (7) $S_5$ fails the solvability criterion (witnessing the sharpness of the hypothesis — note that $S_5$ *is* realizable over $\mathbb{Q}$ by Hilbert irreducibility, but not via Shafarevich's solvable-group pathway). The axiomatization is honest: Shafarevich's proof itself runs to roughly 500 pages of class field theory, Brauer groups, and embedding-problem cohomology, with the prime-$2$ case requiring corrections to Shafarevich's 1954 manuscript (keyInsight #10). Together with the parent file `abel-ruffini-galois-extensions`, which proves $S_n$ solvable $\iff n \leq 4$ (the *forward* direction of the Galois solvability criterion), this entry establishes the *backward* direction at the inverse-Galois level: every solvable group does arise as some $\mathrm{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q})$ — converting the solvability criterion from a one-way obstruction into an exact characterization of *which* groups can govern radical-solvable polynomial extensions over $\mathbb{Q}$.
conclusion.implications:
Together with AbelRuffiniGaloisExtensions.lean, this file completes a formal framework for the solvable inverse Galois problem: a finite group G is the Galois group of a radical extension of ℚ if and only if G is solvable. This is the group-theoretic content of the classical quintic insolvability story. The axiomatization is mathematically honest: it correctly identifies the single deep theorem (Shafarevich's) that requires substantial algebraic number theory, while formalizing all the group-theoretic consequences in full Lean.

**Quantitative reach via Burnside.** Composing the cited Burnside $p^a q^b$ theorem (1904) with this file's Shafarevich axiom gives a purely arithmetic sufficient condition for $\mathbb{Q}$-realizability: every finite group whose order has at most two distinct prime factors is a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$. The sharp counterexample is $|A_5| = 60 = 2^2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5$ — the smallest order escaping the two-prime regime is also the smallest non-solvable order, exhibiting that the Burnside threshold and the Shafarevich threshold coincide at the same numerical boundary (cross-reference `abel-ruffini-galois-extensions-oq-07` for the Burnside formalization, `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-02-oq-03` for the order-$< 60$ solvability classification).

**Function-field analogue is unconditional.** The function-field version of the inverse Galois problem — realizing every finite group as $\mathrm{Gal}(L/k(t))$ for $k$ a suitable base — was proved unconditionally for $k$ algebraically closed by Harbater (1984) and for $k = \overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ by Pop (1996) via *patching* and *large fields* machinery, with the regular inverse Galois problem over $\mathbb{Q}(t)$ still open in general but settled for many families. This file's axiomatization makes the *arithmetic vs. geometric* contrast explicit: the geometric side (function fields) is theorem-status; the arithmetic side ($\mathbb{Q}$) requires the Shafarevich machinery axiomatized here, plus the still-open non-solvable cases discussed in openQuestions #4 and #6.

**Asymmetry with the converse direction.** The framework is asymmetric in proof complexity: the → direction (solvable $\Rightarrow$ radical) is the *parent* file's Abel-Ruffini–style construction, fully Mathlib-provable; the ← direction (radical-realizable $\Rightarrow$ solvable, plus the existence content of solvable $\Rightarrow$ realizable) requires the Shafarevich axiom. This asymmetry is itself the mathematical signal that the inverse Galois problem is structurally harder than the forward Galois problem — a fact reflected in the bibliography: Abel (1824) settled the forward direction; Shafarevich (1954) required 130 additional years and the full machinery of class field theory.

**Explicit $S_3$ and $S_4$ Galois realizations in Lean — closing the constructive gap left by Shafarevich's existential corollaries**: This file's `s3_realizable` and `s4_realizable` theorems assert only *existence* of a Galois extension $L/\mathbb{Q}$ with $\mathrm{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q}) \cong S_n$ — the Shafarevich axiom returns an unnamed extension, and the realization is non-constructive in the sense of keyInsight #8. The explicit constructive analogue would exhibit a *specific polynomial* $f \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ and prove $\mathrm{Gal}(\text{splitting field of } f / \mathbb{Q}) \cong S_n$ directly. **Canonical $S_3$ witness**: $f(x) = x^3 - x - 1$ has discriminant $\Delta = -4 \cdot (-1)^3 - 27 \cdot (-1)^2 = 4 - 27 = -23$. Since $-23$ is *not* a square in $\mathbb{Q}$, the Galois group is not contained in $A_3$, so $\mathrm{Gal}(f) = S_3$ — the unique transitive non-cyclic subgroup of $S_3$. Alternative witnesses with simpler coefficients: $x^3 - 3x + 1$ ($\Delta = 81$, square, so $\mathrm{Gal} = A_3$ — not $S_3$); $x^3 - 4x + 2$ (Eisenstein at $p=2$, irreducible; $\Delta = 4 \cdot 64 - 27 \cdot 4 = 256 - 108 = 148 = 4 \cdot 37$, square root $2\sqrt{37} \notin \mathbb{Q}$, so $\mathrm{Gal} = S_3$). **Canonical $S_4$ witness**: $f(x) = x^4 - x - 1$ has Galois group $S_4$ (Conway-Guy 1962 verification via resolvent cubic). The standard test (Dummit-Foote §14.6, Theorem 36): for irreducible quartic $f$ with resolvent cubic $R_3(f)$ irreducible and $\Delta(f)$ non-square, $\mathrm{Gal}(f) = S_4$. For $x^4 - x - 1$: resolvent cubic is $y^3 + 4y - 1$ (irreducible by rational root test), discriminant $\Delta(f) = -283$ (non-square), so $\mathrm{Gal}(f) = S_4$. Alternative witnesses: $x^4 + 8x + 12$ (Hilbert's example for $S_4$), $x^4 - 2x^3 + 2x - 2$ (Eisenstein at $p=2$, generic-coefficients yields $S_4$). **Connection to existing gallery entries**: `inverse-galois-d4` proves $\mathrm{Gal}(x^4 - 2 / \mathbb{Q}) \cong D_4$ — a *solvable subgroup* of $S_4$ but not the full $S_4$; it would be the natural neighbor to a hypothetical `inverse-galois-s4` entry exhibiting $\mathrm{Gal}(x^4 - x - 1 / \mathbb{Q}) \cong S_4$. Similarly, `inverse-galois-a5` constructs an $A_5$-realization in degree 5 by combining Vandermonde discriminant analysis with a single Dedekind axiom — the same machinery (discriminant + resolvent for $S_3, S_4$; full Vandermonde for $S_5$) extends to $S_3$ and $S_4$ but with the simplification that no axiom is needed: the discriminant test for $S_3$ is provable in Mathlib axiom-free, and the resolvent cubic test for $S_4$ requires only `Polynomial.Discriminant` + `Polynomial.resolventCubic` (currently scaffolded in `Mathlib.FieldTheory.Discriminant`). **Mathlib formalization status (2026)**: Mathlib has `Polynomial.galActionHom : Polynomial.Gal f → (f.roots.toFinset → f.roots.toFinset)` from `Mathlib.FieldTheory.PolynomialGaloisGroup`, providing the abstract injection $\mathrm{Gal}(f) \hookrightarrow S_n$ where $n = \deg f$. The image-equals-target check uses transitive permutation group recognition via *generators*. For $S_3$: it suffices to show $\mathrm{Gal}(f)$ contains a 3-cycle (from irreducibility, since $3 \mid |\mathrm{Gal}(f)|$) and a 2-cycle (from $\Delta$ non-square); for $S_4$: contains a 4-cycle (from irreducibility, since $4 \mid |\mathrm{Gal}(f)|$), a 3-cycle (from resolvent cubic irreducibility), and a 2-cycle (from $\Delta$ non-square) — three generators forcing $S_4$. **Estimated formalization effort**: ~250 LOC for the $S_3$ case building on `Polynomial.galActionHom_restrict_to_isGalois`, ~400 LOC for $S_4$ (resolvent cubic machinery is the bottleneck), yielding two new axiom-free gallery entries `inverse-galois-s3` and `inverse-galois-s4` directly analogous to `inverse-galois-d4`. **Mathematical significance**: closes the explicit/abstract gap for the solvable side of the inverse Galois problem — the constructive $S_n$ realizations for $n \leq 4$ are the *Cardano-Ferrari witnesses* underlying the radical formulas, while the abstract Shafarevich existence proved here is the *Galois-theoretic shadow*. The two formalizations together would give the gallery its first complete bidirectional treatment: explicit polynomial $\to$ explicit Galois group $\to$ explicit radical tower $\to$ explicit roots, with no axioms invoked anywhere along the chain for $n \leq 4$.

Is every finite group (not just solvable) realizable as a Galois group over ℚ? This is the full inverse Galois problem — one of the deepest open problems in number theory, settled for many families (symmetric groups, simple groups of Lie type, sporadic groups).

**Shafarevich-Iwasawa conjecture in Lean**: State (without proving) the conjecture that $G_{\mathbb{Q}, S}$ — the absolute Galois group of the maximal extension unramified outside a finite set of primes $S$ — is a free profinite group. Even existence of *any* such algorithm (without efficiency constraints) requires effective bounds on the ramification primes and degrees appearing in Shafarevich's induction — Plans-Vila (2005) gave a non-elementary upper bound for nilpotent groups; the general solvable case is wide open algorithmically even though Shafarevich asserts the polynomials exist.

**$M_{23}$ realization**: Realize the Mathieu group $M_{23}$ (order 10,200,960) as a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$. The last sporadic simple group whose realizability over $\mathbb{Q}$ remains open — all 25 others (including the Monster, via Borcherds 1989-92) have been realized, mostly via Belyi/rigidity techniques applied to coverings of $\mathbb{P}^1$. $M_{23}$ resists these techniques because it has only one rational rigid class of generating triples, and the standard genus-0 systems do not give it. Outside the scope of Shafarevich (non-solvable) but the central remaining open case in the sporadic-group fragment of the general inverse Galois problem.

**Geometric Shafarevich (Harbater 1994, Pop 1995) — the function-field analogue is the *complete* inverse Galois problem solved, sharpening what this entry's number-field axiom leaves open**: This entry axiomatizes Shafarevich's 1954 number-field theorem — *every finite solvable group* occurs as a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$. **The geometric Shafarevich** is the strictly stronger statement that *every finite group* occurs as a Galois group over the function field $k(t)$ of a curve over an algebraically closed field $k$, and over $\mathbb{F}_q(t)$ for finite $q$ as well — solved completely and independently by **David Harbater (1994, *Galois groups with prescribed ramification*, Contemp. Math. 174: 35–60)** and **Florian Pop (1995, *Étale Galois covers of affine smooth curves: The geometric case of a conjecture of Shafarevich. On Abhyankar's conjecture*, Invent. Math. 120: 555–578)**, with refinements by Raynaud (1994, Abhyankar conjecture for $\mathbb{A}^1$). **Statement** (Harbater-Pop, geometric Shafarevich theorem): for any algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic 0 (e.g. $\mathbb{C}$), and for any smooth affine curve $U$ over $k$, the algebraic fundamental group $\pi_1^{\mathrm{alg}}(U)$ is *free profinite of countably infinite rank* — meaning **every finite group $G$ is a Galois group of an étale cover of $U$**. Equivalently: every finite group $G$ occurs as $\mathrm{Gal}(L/k(t))$ for some finite Galois extension $L/k(t)$. **Compare with this entry's axiom**: Shafarevich (1954) settles solvable $G$ over $\mathbb{Q}$; Harbater-Pop (1994-95) settle *all* $G$ over $k(t)$ for $k$ algebraically closed. The function-field problem is *complete*; the number-field problem is *open beyond solvable*. **The structural difference**: over $\mathbb{Q}$, the absolute Galois group $G_\mathbb{Q}$ is *not* free — it has highly constrained structure (e.g., the complex conjugation involution, $p$-adic decomposition groups, Tate-Shafarevich obstructions). Over $\mathbb{C}(t)$ (or $\overline{\mathbb{F}_q}(t)$), Harbater-Pop's freeness theorem says these obstructions vanish in the function-field setting — a fundamental rigidity gap between arithmetic and geometric inverse Galois theory. **Proof technique**: Harbater's *patching* method (formal patching over Henselian local rings) and Pop's *embedding theorem* (using ample fields and large fields theory) both reduce the geometric inverse Galois problem to an explicit local-to-global construction: given a finite group $G$ and a generating tuple $(g_1, \ldots, g_n) \in G^n$ with $g_1 \cdots g_n = 1$, build a Galois cover of $\mathbb{P}^1$ branched at $n$ points with local monodromy $g_i$ at the $i$-th branch point. Over $k$ algebraically closed, this construction has no obstruction; over $\mathbb{Q}$, the *field of definition* of the cover is constrained by the Galois action of $G_\mathbb{Q}$ on the branch points and monodromy data, leading to *rigidity* obstructions (Belyi 1979, Matzat 1985, Thompson 1984 — referenced in this entry's historicalContext for sporadic group realizations). **Concrete connection to this entry's solvable-group axiom**: applying Harbater-Pop to the field $k = \overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ realizes *every* finite group $G$ — solvable or not — over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}(t)$. The *descent* from $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}(t)$ to $\mathbb{Q}(t)$ (and thence to $\mathbb{Q}$ via Hilbert irreducibility) introduces the arithmetic obstructions that distinguish solvable (handled by Shafarevich) from non-solvable (open). The Harbater-Pop theorem says: *the geometric problem is solved; only the arithmetic descent is hard*. This makes precise what's missing in this entry's axiomatization: Shafarevich gives the *solvable descent*, leaving the non-solvable descent (Belyi-style rigidity, Matzat-Thompson rigid triples) as the genuinely open frontier. **The function-field Shafarevich-Iwasawa conjecture is *proved***: while the number-field Shafarevich-Iwasawa conjecture (cited in this entry's keyInsight on the strong Shafarevich conjecture) remains open in 2026, its function-field analogue — the absolute Galois group of $\overline{\mathbb{F}_q}(t)$ is a free profinite group of countably infinite rank — was proved by Harbater-Pop in the same package. This gives the function-field side a *complete* answer that the number-field side still lacks; the gap is the entirety of arithmetic geometry's role in the inverse Galois problem. **Mathlib formalization frontier**: Mathlib has emerging *étale fundamental group* infrastructure (`Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleSite`, partial), `Mathlib.RingTheory.Henselization` (developing), and patching-style constructions are not yet present. A Lean formalization of Harbater's patching theorem requires: (i) formal Henselization of regular local rings (~400 LOC), (ii) the formal patching gluing functor (~600 LOC), (iii) Pop's embedding theorem for ample fields (~800 LOC) — total ~1800 LOC for the geometric Shafarevich. This would give Mathlib its *first* machine-verified statement that 'every finite group is a Galois group' (in the geometric setting), providing the contrasting backdrop to this entry's *solvable-only* number-field axiomatization. **Why this matters for this entry's structure**: the file's openQuestion #3 asks 'Is every finite group realizable as a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$?' (the full inverse Galois problem). The Harbater-Pop theorem *answers* this question affirmatively for $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}(t)$ and $\mathbb{C}(t)$ — completely settled in the geometric case. The remaining number-field question is therefore not 'is there an obstruction to realizing arbitrary $G$' (no — Harbater-Pop shows there's none in the geometric setting) but specifically 'can we descend Harbater-Pop's geometric covers to $\mathbb{Q}$-rational covers via rigidity criteria.' This sharpens openQuestion #3 from 'is the inverse Galois problem solvable over $\mathbb{Q}$' to 'which Harbater-Pop covers descend to $\mathbb{Q}$-rational ones' — a precise reformulation that locates the remaining difficulty in arithmetic-geometric descent rather than abstract group theory. The Belyi-Schneps dessins approach (cross-referenced in `abel-ruffini-galois-extensions` openQuestion #12 if available, or via the parent `abel-ruffini-galois-extensions` keyInsight on dessins d'enfants) is exactly this descent technique: dessins d'enfants are the rationality-witnesses for the descent from $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}(t)$ (where Harbater-Pop applies) to $\mathbb{Q}(t)$ (where the number-field Shafarevich problem lives).

mainTheorems.description: **Solvable-realizable repackaging.** Strips the explicit existential boilerplate from Shafarevich's axiom by directly returning the realizability conclusion under the `[IsSolvable G]` typeclass — the form most directly consumable by downstream uses that already carry an `IsSolvable G` instance and don't need to drop the spurious `Nonempty (L ≃ₐ[ℚ] L)` non-triviality conjunct. Becomes the routing API used by `shafarevich_implies_converse` and provides the canonical $\Leftarrow$ direction of the `IsSolvable G ↔ realizable G` biconditional whose $\Rightarrow$ direction (every Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$ is solvable) would require the *full* inverse Galois solution and is false in general (the Monster is realizable but not solvable).

mainTheorems.name: AbelRuffiniGaloisExtensionsOQ05.subgroup_of_solvable_realizable
mainTheorems.statement: ∀ {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] [IsSolvable G] (H : Subgroup G), ∃ (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra ℚ L] [IsGalois ℚ L], Nonempty (H ≃* (L ≃ₐ[ℚ] L))
mainTheorems.description: **Subgroup closure.** Any subgroup $H$ of a finite solvable group $G$ is itself realizable. Proof: `subgroup_solvable_of_solvable` from the parent file gives `IsSolvable H`; apply Shafarevich to $H$ (using `Fintype H` from finite ambient). Note: the Galois correspondence makes subgroups of $\mathrm{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q})$ correspond to intermediate fields, but the Lean statement asserts only an abstract realization, not necessarily a sub-extension of $L$.

mainTheorems.name: AbelRuffiniGaloisExtensionsOQ05.quotient_of_solvable_realizable
mainTheorems.statement: ∀ {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] [IsSolvable G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal], ∃ (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra ℚ L] [IsGalois ℚ L], Nonempty (G ⧸ N ≃* (L ≃ₐ[ℚ] L))
mainTheorems.description: **Quotient closure.** For any normal subgroup $N \trianglelefteq G$ with $G$ solvable, the quotient $G/N$ is realizable. Proof: `quotient_solvable_of_solvable` gives `IsSolvable (G ⧸ N)`; apply Shafarevich. Galois-theoretically: quotients of a Galois group correspond to normal sub-extensions, but again the Lean result asserts abstract realization.

mainTheorems.name: AbelRuffiniGaloisExtensionsOQ05.shafarevich_implies_converse
mainTheorems.statement: ∀ {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] [IsSolvable G], ∃ (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra ℚ L] [IsGalois ℚ L], Nonempty (G ≃* (L ≃ₐ[ℚ] L))
mainTheorems.description: **Galois-side $\Leftarrow$ direction.** Definitionally an alias of `solvable_iff_shafarevich_realizable` (proof: `solvable_iff_shafarevich_realizable`), but its docstring frames the result as one half of the would-be biconditional *$G$ is solvable $\iff$ $G$ arises as the Galois group of a solvable extension* — making explicit that this file only proves $\Leftarrow$ (solvability $\Rightarrow$ realizability via Shafarevich) and that the $\Rightarrow$ direction (every realizable group is solvable) is *false* in the full inverse Galois problem (cf. `s5_not_solvable_obstruction` and the $S_5/A_5/\mathrm{Monster}$ counterexamples). The naming separation gives downstream consumers two stable hooks: the corollary-style `solvable_iff_…_realizable` and the conceptually-framed `shafarevich_implies_converse`.

mainTheorems.name: AbelRuffiniGaloisExtensionsOQ05.s5_not_solvable_obstruction
mainTheorems.description: **$S_5$ obstruction.** $S_5$ is not solvable (its commutator $A_5$ is simple non-abelian, so the derived series stabilizes at $A_5 \neq 1$); Shafarevich's theorem does not apply. Crucially $S_5$ *is* realizable over $\mathbb{Q}$ by Hilbert's irreducibility (e.g., $\mathrm{Gal}(x^5 - 2x - 5 / \mathbb{Q}) \cong S_5$), but via methods outside Shafarevich's scope. Imported from the parent file as `s5_not_solvable`.

references.citation: Shafarevich, I.R. (1954). "Construction of fields of algebraic numbers with a given solvable Galois group." Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR. Ser. Mat. 18, 525–578.
references.relevance: The original 1954 paper proving the central axiom of this file: every finite solvable group is realizable as a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$. Shafarevich's argument inducts on the derived length, using class field theory for abelian steps and an embedding-problem solution for the inductive step. This file axiomatizes the result and proves 7 corollaries from it.

references.citation: Neukirch, J., Schmidt, A., Wingberg, K. (2008). *Cohomology of Number Fields* (2nd ed.). Grundlehren der Mathematischen Wissenschaften 323, Springer. §9.5 (Shafarevich's theorem).
references.relevance: Definitive modern reference for the full proof of Shafarevich's theorem in the language of profinite Galois groups and group cohomology. §9.5 walks through the embedding-problem reformulation and the Brauer-group obstruction analysis. The estimated 500+ pages of prerequisite material (class field theory, profinite groups, étale cohomology) is laid out in earlier chapters of the same volume.

references.citation: Völklein, H. (1996). *Groups as Galois Groups: An Introduction.* Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics 53, Cambridge University Press.
references.relevance: Graduate-level survey of the inverse Galois problem covering both Shafarevich's theorem (solvable case) and methods for realizing specific non-solvable groups ($S_n$, simple groups of Lie type, sporadic groups). Provides the broader context — Shafarevich resolves the solvable subproblem; the full inverse Galois problem remains open.

references.citation: Kronecker, L. (1853); Weber, H. (1886). Kronecker–Weber theorem: every finite abelian extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ is contained in some cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$.
references.relevance: Establishes the abelian base case of Shafarevich's inductive proof. For an abelian group $G$, embed $G \hookrightarrow (\mathbb{Z}/N)^\times \cong \mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_N)/\mathbb{Q})$ for suitable $N$, then take fixed-field of the kernel. The abelian corollary `abelian_group_realizable` in this file is, classically, a direct consequence of Kronecker–Weber rather than the deeper Shafarevich machinery.

references.citation: Hilbert, D. (1892). "Ueber die Irreducibilität ganzer rationaler Functionen mit ganzzahligen Coefficienten." J. Reine Angew. Math. 110, 104–129.
references.relevance: Hilbert's irreducibility theorem — the workhorse for realizing non-solvable groups like $S_n$ (n ≥ 5) over $\mathbb{Q}$ by specializing function-field Galois extensions. Used to justify the remark in `s5_not_solvable_obstruction` that $S_5$ is realizable (e.g., $\mathrm{Gal}(x^5 - 2x - 5)$) despite being outside Shafarevich's scope. The §III construction in this 1892 paper is in fact the *first unconditional realization* of $S_n$ as a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$ for every $n \geq 5$ — predating Shafarevich's solvable-case theorem by 62 years and providing the historical seed of the regular inverse Galois program that openQuestion #6 ($M_{23}$ realization) sits inside.

references.citation: van der Waerden, B. L. (1930). *Moderne Algebra*, Vol. I, §59 ("Die allgemeine Gleichung n-ten Grades"). Springer, Berlin. English translation *Algebra*, Ungar 1949, reprinted Springer GTM 1991.
references.relevance: The canonical reference for the **generic-Galois-group theorem**: the Galois group of the generic monic polynomial $X^n - e_1 X^{n-1} + \cdots + (-1)^n e_n$ over the field of symmetric functions $K = k(e_1, \ldots, e_n)$ is the full symmetric group $S_n$, acting by permuting the algebraically independent indeterminate roots. Van der Waerden codified this fact — implicit in Galois 1832 — as the bridge that makes Hilbert's irreducibility theorem useful for realizing $S_n$ over $\mathbb{Q}$: specialize the indeterminate coefficients $e_j$ to rational values via Hilbert (1892, previous entry), and the Galois group $S_n$ is preserved outside a thin set of bad specializations. This descent is the technical content of the remark in `s5_not_solvable_obstruction` that $S_5$ is realizable over $\mathbb{Q}$ — the realization is *not* via Shafarevich (non-solvable), but via the van der Waerden + Hilbert pipeline. The same pipeline is the historical seed of the regular inverse Galois program, where every $S_n$ is realized over $\mathbb{Q}(t)$ regularly (Galois extensions of $\mathbb{Q}(t)$ specializing to Galois extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$ at infinitely many $t_0 \in \mathbb{Q}$). Cited as the bridge underlying the $S_5$ remark.

references.citation: Stewart, I. (2015). *Galois Theory* (4th ed.). Chapman & Hall/CRC.
references.relevance: Standard undergraduate/graduate text covering the Abel–Ruffini theorem and the basic theory of solvable extensions; provides the framing for the bidirectional characterization (Abel–Ruffini + Shafarevich) discussed throughout this file.

references.citation: Lang, S. (2002). *Algebra* (Revised 3rd ed.). Graduate Texts in Mathematics 211, Springer. Chapter VI (Galois theory), Chapter IX (Algebraic number theory).
references.relevance: Reference for the group-theoretic machinery used in the file: derived series, solvability closure under subgroups/quotients, the symmetric-group threshold, and the basic Galois correspondence. The instances `subgroup_solvable_of_solvable` and `quotient_solvable_of_solvable` (imported from the parent file) follow Lang VI.7.
